title: Tvcache: A Tool-Value Cache for Post-Training LLM Agents
claim: Tool calls take a large share of rollout time and repeat across rollouts, leaving expensive GPUs idle and motivating caching.
layout: Timeline of 4 rollout rows, top to bottom, with arrows into a sandbox box
description: The top legend marks reasoning in green and tool calls in orange. Below it, four horizontal rows labeled Rollouts 1–4 are timelines of alternating green and orange blocks. Time runs left to right along an arrow underneath. GPU 0 and GPU 1 labels sit on the right edge and span pairs of rows. The orange blocks, some of them wide, make up a large share of each row, so tool execution dominates the timeline. Orange arrows run from four of Rollout 4's tool-call blocks to a bold, black-outlined box labeled 'Rollout 4 Sandbox'. Inside it, orange command boxes read 'set terminal env; download deps', 'git clone code; check deps', 'apply bug fix; compile' and 'run tests'. The eye goes first to the green and orange stripes, then follows the arrows down to the sandbox.
caption: Illustration of 4 rollouts from an RL post-training iteration over time. The tokens generated in each rollout interleave between reasoning (green) and tool-calling (orange). Tools are executed in a sandbox environment and may mutate the sandbox state. In practice, tool execution comprises a significant portion of post-training time. \sysname maps tool outputs to tool calls in addition to a graph-based representation of the sandbox state to eliminate redundant tool executions and speed up post-training.
abstract: In RL post-training of LLM agents, calls to external tools take several seconds or even minutes, leaving allocated GPUs idle and inflating post-training time and cost. While many tool invocations repeat across parallel rollouts and could in principle be cached, naively caching their outputs for reuse is incorrect since tool outputs depend on the environment state induced by prior agent interactions. We present TVCACHE, a stateful tool-value cache for LLM agent post-training. TVCACHE maintains a tree of observed tool-call sequences and performs longest-prefix matching for cache lookups: a hit occurs only when the agent's full tool history matches a previously executed sequence, guaranteeing identical environment state. On three diverse workloads-terminal-based tasks, SQL generation, and video understanding. TVCACHE achieves cache hit rates of up to 70% and reduces median tool call execution time by up to 6.9X, with no degradation in post-training reward accumulation.
